candidates.detail: InventoryItemId publicly wraps u64, Inventory::get_mut exposes each item and its public id, and Inventory::validate checks duplicate IDs and article validity without excluding u64::MAX. Inventory::add adds one to every existing ID before selecting the maximum. A valid inventory containing an otherwise valid article with ID u64::MAX therefore reaches an unrepresentable addition; overflow-checked builds panic, while unchecked arithmetic wraps. For example, with existing distinct IDs u64::MAX and u64::MAX-1, unchecked wrapping makes the latter successor u64::MAX and can publish a duplicate of the first. This is source and unsigned arithmetic reasoning only: no inventory, recipe, JSON, UI or product ran.

candidates.detail: WornGraph::support checks a matching point against children already in its graph. While attaching one candidate, WornGraph::attach calls support separately for each parent requirement, then adds the number of this same candidate's earlier edges on the point to the returned slot index without rechecking capacity. With one matching capacity-1 point, zero graph children and two matching requirements on the candidate, the source yields prospective slot indices 0 and 1. EquipmentGraph::equip checks edge uniqueness, existing edge conflicts, parent presence and cycles, but receives no catalog capacity; distinct slots 0 and 1 do not trigger those checks. The first failing contract is prospective capacity reservation, not duplicate slot detection. This is source and integer reasoning only; no catalog, graph or product ran.
candidates.consumer_and_safeguards: Inventory::fit resolves catalog placements and builds this WornGraph; successful fit is used by wear and loadout. EquipmentPlacement stores a vector of parent requirements, the selected dependency validator parses them independently, and attachment point validation allows capacity 1. The creator ItemCatalog::new checks armor recipes rather than establishing this prospective graph invariant.
